sections.label: Planning Act amendment aims
sections.summary: The passage states three aims: enhancing URA planning levers, strengthening development plan regulation with penalties, and simplifying administrative processes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, to enhance the planning levers for URA to ensure a more liveable city; second, to strengthen the regulatory regime for development plans, including penalties to deal with violations of planning controls; and third, to calibrate and simplify the administrative processes involved in the execution of the Act.

sections.label: Penalties for unauthorised development
sections.summary: It sets enhanced penalties including custodial sentences for repeat offenders, unauthorised dormitory use, and conserved building demolition, with an owner presumption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The maximum penalty for unauthorised development, works or subdivision for repeat offenders or for an offence involving the unauthorised use of any land or building for dormitory accommodation will be enhanced to include a custodial sentence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The maximum penalty for the partial or full demolition of a conserved building is a fine of $500,000 or a custodial sentence, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: An owner is presumed to have permitted unauthorised works carried out by his tenants or contractors, unless the owner can show that reasonable precaution was taken to prevent this.

sections.label: Residential property use restrictions
sections.summary: A new Schedule lists short-term and dormitory accommodation as illegal without permission, defining dormitory accommodation as seven or more persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Where private residential properties are rented or sublet, URA has existing guidelines in place to ensure that these properties are not used to accommodate excessive numbers of occupants, and to make it clear that such properties are intended for long-term or permanent residence of at least six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This Bill inserts a new Schedule into the Act, which lists the uses of residential property that are illegal without permission.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The uses listed are short-term accommodation and dormitory accommodation. "Dormitory accommodation", which requires planning permission, is defined by the Bill to mean accommodation by seven or more persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In other words, without planning permission, it will be illegal to have more than six tenants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For units currently housing seven or eight persons, URA will allow the tenancy agreements to run their natural course and will not clamp down on them before they expire.

sections.label: Preserving heritage buildings' spirit
sections.summary: The passage asks how to protect conserved buildings and create a cityscape celebrating built heritage, seeking the Minister's response on preserving their inner spirit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As the Bill hopes to give powers to both afford greater protection against unauthorised demolition or alterations to conserved buildings, and at the same time, create a delightful cityscape, we might have to ask ourselves how we can best achieve most in creating the cityscape that incorporates and, in fact, celebrates our built heritage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Whether by private hands or in the public interest, historic buildings are sometimes disappearing, not just physically but also slowly being drained of their souls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, I seek the Minister's response on how best we should, not just as a government, but as custodians of our nation's collective storehouse of memories and history, preserve not just the shell of buildings but also the inner spirit and souls of our heritage buildings.

sections.label: Stronger heritage destruction penalties
sections.summary: The passage says the Bill introduces custodial sentences and higher fines, but suggests stripping licences and educating Singaporeans on built heritage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Planning (Amendment) Bill sends a stronger signal with a custodial sentence being introduced, and the fine imposed being raised, but losing our heritage cannot be adequately compensated by a jail-term or half a million dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We need more than that, perhaps a stripping away of the licence of the developer or contractor involved in the destruction but, more importantly, also to educate Singaporeans on the importance of our built heritage.

sections.label: Custodial sentence and HDB subtenants
sections.summary: It states a custodial sentence is introduced for infringements, and that 4-room and larger HDB flats allow nine subtenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A custodial sentence is also introduced for infringements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In 4-room and larger HDB flats, the number of subtenants allowed is nine.

sections.label: Short-term lease minimum and subtenants
sections.summary: Existing subtenants above six may let leases lapse, and a six-month minimum for short-term accommodation leases matches HDB sub-leasing rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In terms of the new limitations, I am happy to learn from the Minister that those that already have more than six subtenants will be allowed to have their leases lapse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In terms of now legislating the minimum six months for short-term accommodation leases, this brings it in line with HDB sub-leasing requirements.

sections.label: Offence for missing written permission
sections.summary: The new subsection (3)(ca) makes failure to obtain written permission an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With the insertion of the new subsection (3)(ca), failure to obtain written permission for this will be an offence.

sections.label: URA enforcement and complaint figures
sections.summary: URA enforcement cases for unauthorised short-term subletting were 36 in 2014, 23 in 2015 and 44 in early 2016, far below complaints received.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Minister had shared with the House in a written reply in August last year that URA took enforcement action against 36 cases of unauthorised short-term subletting in private residential premises in 2014, 23 cases in 2015, and 44 cases in the first six months of 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These figures are very much lower than the number of complaints received by URA − 375 in 2014, 377 in 2015 and 161 in the first four months of 2016.

sections.label: MCST power for enforcement
sections.summary: An uneasy estate atmosphere harms neighbourly ties, so the Minister is asked to consider giving the MCST more power and means for enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Such an uneasy atmosphere in an estate does not contribute to building neighbourly ties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to suggest that the Minister consider giving the Management Corporation Strata Title (MCST) more power and greater means at its disposal for enforcement.

sections.label: Maximum residents in HDB and private housing
sections.summary: Four-room and bigger HDB units may house up to nine persons and private housing six, and the speaker urges a maximum of six for HDB too.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, for 4-room and bigger HDB units, the maximum number of persons residing is a maximum of nine people.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For private housing, it is six persons, but for HDB flats, which is even more compact, can house up to nine.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I urge that this maximum number be whittled down to no more than six persons also.

sections.label: Online listings count
sections.summary: The speaker understood there are about 6,000 listings online.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What I understood is that there are about 6,000 listings online.

sections.label: Short-term rentals and subletting limits
sections.summary: The passage proposes allowing short-term rentals if residents agree, covered linkways for condominiums and ECs, and reducing the maximum unrelated subletters from eight to six.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, we can allow short-term rentals for certain apartments, as long as all the residents are agreeable to it.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, I hope that this amendment Bill will allow residents living in condominiums and ECs to enjoy covered linkways which connect their condominium or EC to the nearest bus-stop, just like HDB residents do.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, with our limited land, urban planning is crucial to maintain a good quality of life and have good quality buildings.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this age of rapid developments, it is important that we frequently review the rules and update them whenever necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The first is regarding the reduction of the permissible maximum number of unrelated persons for subletting, from the current eight to six persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The universal cap of six persons per unit may not be optimal.

sections.label: Dormitory and short-term accommodation use
sections.summary: Providing dormitory accommodation for seven or more persons or short-term accommodation of six consecutive months or less for rent is deemed a change of use requiring written permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Next, on the provision of dormitory accommodation for seven or more persons and short-term accommodation of six consecutive months or less for rent will be deemed a change of use for a dwelling-house for which failure to obtain written permission will be an offence.

sections.label: Due diligence steps for owners
sections.summary: The speaker suggests section 12A could list due diligence steps for owners, such as requesting a tenant or contractor to sign an undertaking or statutory declaration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In my view, section 12A could be more prescriptive in listing out the due diligence steps that owners should take, such as requesting the tenant or contractor to sign an undertaking or affirm a statutory declaration.

sections.label: Airbnb and short-term lease rules
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore needs to embrace disruptive technologies like Airbnb, notes the Bill prohibits short-term leases to many unrelated persons, and asks about licensing vacation homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding, Singapore also needs to embrace disruptive technologies or emerging opportunities, such as Airbnb and others, especially in an environment of softer growth and to capitalise on existing unproductive assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, I am pleased that it is now spelt out in the Bill the rules that prohibit short-term lease to a large number of unrelated persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps, it would be good if the Minister could clarify what its policy will be on Airbnb going forward, if the owner of a premises applies for a licence to use it for vacation homes, for example?

sections.label: URA powers over building design
sections.summary: URA has been given more decision-making power over building appearance and design to make Singapore delightful and walkable, raising questions about development costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Next, I note that URA has been given more power in the decision-making process with regard to the physical appearance and design of buildings, with the goal of making Singapore a delightful and walkable city in relation to the latest rule on public spaces on private property to meet new design guidelines, such as providing ample shade, public seating and connectivity between buildings either above or below ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But the question is: how will this affect the cost of development for the building owner?

sections.label: Amendment covers private properties only
sections.summary: The amendment refers only to private properties and not HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: One, in this amendment, it only refers to private properties and not HDB flats.

sections.label: HDB owner checks and rental rules
sections.summary: HDB could not locate owners or check suspected units, so the speaker suggests occupancy rules based on built-up area and contactable owner details.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: HDB had difficulties locating the owners, especially those who live overseas, and were unable to conduct the appropriate checks of the suspected units.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I suggest that the Ministry consider applying the rule on the basis of the number of people per the built-up area, which is the gross floor area regardless of public or private property.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In addition, all owners must be made to provide contactable details when declaring their property for rental and are held accountable if their tenants refuse to cooperate with the authorities.

sections.label: Support for amendment and sections
sections.summary: The speaker supports the amendment and the introduction of sections 13, 19A and 20A.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As such, I support the amendment and the introduction of sections 13, 19A and 20A.

sections.label: QP validation and developer violations
sections.summary: The speaker asks how QP certifications are validated and how violations by QPs or developers are made public.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Before they can reach the stage of obtaining the Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP), it would have entailed legal suits and caused home owners unwarranted stress, notwithstanding the strain it creates in our mediation and litigation systems.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: To reduce the frequency of such incidences, I would like to ask the Minister on the validation process of the QPs, how to ensure their certifications are kept relevant and that these QPs have duly carried out their duties and tasks before they endorse and sign off on the approval documents.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: If the QPs and/or developers were found to have violated the rules, how can it be made known to the public so that future consumers would not fall prey to the unruly players?

sections.label: URA short-term rental consultation
sections.summary: URA said the 2016 public consultation on short-term rentals was split with no clear consensus and needed more study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In May 2016, URA stated that the results of the public consultation on short-term rentals were "split, with no clear consensus".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: URA, by its own admission, added that "this issue on short-term stays is complex, multi-faceted, has wide-ranging implications and it warrants a careful and balanced review," and, therefore, it "needed more time to study the issue".

sections.label: Airbnb ban in Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Singapore wants to ban Airbnb, citing media reports of over a million listings and 25 million guests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Just taking into consideration Airbnb, do we really want to ban a company which, according to some media reports, boasts more than a million listings across 190 countries in 34,000 cities with more than 25 million guests served, from operating in Singapore?

sections.label: Fourth Schedule unrelated persons limit
sections.summary: The speaker notes that under the new Fourth Schedule, URA will reduce the maximum number of unrelated persons a property can be rented to from eight to six.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As echoed by other Members who have spoken earlier on this Bill, I, too, would like to mention that, firstly, under the new Fourth Schedule, URA will reduce the maximum number of unrelated persons a property can be rented to from eight to six.

sections.label: Sub-tenant caps by flat size
sections.summary: Sets sub-tenant limits: four for 1-room and 2-room flats, six for 3-room flats, nine for 4-room and bigger flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For 1-room and 2-room flats, four sub-tenants; for 3-room flats, six sub-tenants; and for 4-room and bigger flats, nine sub-tenants.

sections.label: Owners subletting to multiple tenants
sections.summary: Recent cases involved owners who collected deposits and sublet the same property to multiple tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the last few years, there have been cases of owners who collected deposits and sublet the same property to multiple tenants.

sections.label: URA planning levers for connectivity
sections.summary: The Bill's amendment strengthens URA planning levers, and URA will require developers to provide connectivity and better building standards in new developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And this is what the amendment in the Bill strives to achieve, by strengthening the planning levers under URA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, in response to some of the queries raised by Members, I can confirm that URA will, indeed, make use of these provisions to require developers, where it comes to new developments, to put in place connectivity and better building standards, including more covered linkways between buildings or even to nearby bus stops.

sections.label: Cost of providing features
sections.summary: The cost of providing these features is generally a small component of overall development costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Generally, the cost of providing these features is a small component of the overall development costs.

sections.label: Public spaces excluded from floor area
sections.summary: Required public spaces may be excluded from overall floor area, so development potential of sites would not be affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In addition, the public spaces that are required may be excluded from the overall floor area, so there would be no impact on the development potential of the sites.

sections.label: Members suggest occupancy cap by size
sections.summary: Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggest calibrating the occupancy cap according to residential unit size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggest that the occupancy cap be calibrated according to the size of the residential unit.

sections.label: Reverting to six-person cap
sections.summary: The speaker says alternative accommodation has been built up and it is timely to revert to the cap of six, as before 2008.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Since then, we have built up a good supply of alternative accommodation catering to groups other than families, such as hostels for students and dormitories for company employees and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we believe it is timely to revert to the cap of six, which was what it used to be before 2008.

sections.label: Rise in short-term rental complaints
sections.summary: URA saw a 60% rise in complaints from home owners over the past year about short-term rule breaches, citing nuisance or safety concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Indeed, over the past year, URA has already seen a 60% rise in complaints from home owners about breaches of this short-term rule in their residential properties, and the complaints are related to public nuisance or even safety concerns for their families.

sections.label: MSCTs, enforcement and six-month minimum
sections.summary: MSCTs can take practical steps and assist URA enforcement; the six-month minimum short-term rental period is in the Act's Schedule and can be adjusted by gazette.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: These are meaningful and practical things that MSCTs can do, and we will encourage them to do so and assist URA in its enforcement action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I should also clarify that the minimum period of six months for short-term rental in private residences is set out in the Schedule of the Act, and the Government can adjust this parameter in future by gazette.

sections.label: New use class for short-term rentals
sections.summary: URA is studying creating a new use class for private residences wishing to do short-term rentals, approved for that purpose like serviced apartments or hotels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In this regard, I am happy to share that URA is studying the option of creating a new use class for private residences that wish to engage in short-term rentals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Such properties would then be approved for that specific purpose, like serviced apartments or hotels today.

sections.label: Balancing intervention and property owners' rights
sections.summary: The speaker urges reconsideration, citing balance between intervention and owners' rights, says the Bill's Planning Act amendments do not cover everything, and will continue mediation and study.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: So, this is why I want to urge the Minister to reconsider this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have to balance the need for intervention and action against property owners' rights to their own living spaces and to their own homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Planning Act amendments, as I have said, that are in the Bill, do not cover the full extent of what the Member would like to see.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will continue with the mediation route which we have already been doing and will continue to do more of that, but we will continue to study and see if other things can be done to address these difficult issues between neighbours and between two property owners where there are conflicting issues, like the one that the Member has raised.

sections.label: URA to come up with something soon
sections.summary: The speaker has described broad outlines of approaches being considered and expects URA to come up with something quite soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I have described very broad outlines of some of the approaches that we are thinking about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I would expect URA to be able to come up with something quite soon.
